summary: A notice that UCLA's Network Measurement Center would gather NCP statistics from hosts automatically each day. It opens a connection to a local socket 241 and expects counts such as bits and messages sent and received, plus optional round-trip delay. Results would be published monthly.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC describes how UCLA-NMC will collect NCP traffic statistics from participating hosts. It specifies a daily sample period, the data to report and the format of the report.

questions: what statistics did hosts report to socket 241
what was in the ncp statistics message format
subtitle: A method for hosts to send daily NCP statistics to UCLA-NMC.

tldr.problem: The RFC proposes regular automatic collection of NCP statistics after a five-month lapse since RFC 323.
tldr.mechanism: UCLA-NMC opens a connection to local socket 241 and expects a host to send counts for bits and messages, with optional delay and control-message data.
tldr.outcome: The results were to be published monthly as Network Measurement notes and RFCs, and other hosts were invited to participate.

facts.label: Data connections
facts.value: Standard open connections; link 0 control counts optional

today: The unit metadata lists RFC 388 as Unknown and says it updates RFC 323. The RFC describes a 1972 measurement arrangement.

sections.title: The Collection Procedure
sections.content:
UCLA-NMC announces that it is ready to gather NCP statistics automatically on a daily basis. It will periodically open a connection on a host's local socket 241 (decimal), and expects the host to send its data after receiving an Allocate command.

When transmission of the last message is complete and its RFNM arrives, the host closes the connection. A host that connects to UCLA-NMC socket 241 can receive UCLA-NMC's own 24-hour data.
sections.plainLanguage: UCLA-NMC opens a connection to a host's socket 241 and requests its report. The report covers the last local 24-hour period.

sections.title: Statistics Included
sections.content:
The requested figures include total bits and messages sent to and received from each host, plus an optional average round-trip delay on send connections. The RFC says only standard open connections should be counted, excluding measurement and experimental NCP links; it specifically excludes link 0 from the per-host traffic counts.

An optional report can show the distribution of message types on link 0 across all hosts. The RFC says the summarized figures cover a standard local day, such as local midnight to midnight, rather than a sliding 24-hour period.
sections.plainLanguage: Hosts report how many bits and messages they exchanged with other hosts. They can also report average delay and counts of control-message types.

sections.title: Report Format
sections.content:
The first word contains a 16-bit day number and a 16-bit time in minutes when sampling started. The second word contains the source host, byte size, number of host-related entries and format flags.

Each following entry identifies a foreign host and includes the counts selected by the format flags. Optional link 0 control-message data uses pairs of an 8-bit type and a 24-bit count; average RFNM delay is in milliseconds.
sections.plainLanguage: The report begins with the sample date and time, then identifies the reporting host and which statistics follow. It then lists data for each other host.

sections.title: Participation and Publication
sections.content: The RFC says UCLA-NMC will publish results monthly as Network Measurement notes and RFCs. UCLA-NMC, DMCG and LL-67 are named as participants, and other hosts are invited to join.
sections.plainLanguage: Several sites are named as participants, and other hosts are invited. UCLA-NMC plans to publish the collected results each month.

viz.caption: FIRST TWO WORDS OF THE REPORT (RFC 388)

fields.name: Day number
fields.desc: Day of year: 1 to 365, or 6 on leap year.

fields.name: Start time
fields.desc: Minutes at which sample started, from 0 to 1439.

fields.name: Source host
fields.desc: Network host number of the reporter.

fields.name: Byte size
fields.desc: Bits per byte in byte statistics.

fields.name: Format
fields.desc: Flags C, R, B and M select optional contents.

references.text: RFC 323, the earlier request for NCP statistics.
